claim: Defaults raise uptake of the default option in humans: automatic 401(k) enrolment gave 86% participation vs 37% at matched tenure; meta-analytic default d about 0.62.
agent_test: Add a pre-filled answer to the prompt vs none; measure copy rate at equal tokens.
note: d07 original read: d 0.68 (0.53-0.83), 58 studies, n 73,675; 27 pp on binary outcomes.

claim: A default carries its details too: 76% of auto-enrolled participants kept the 3% rate and 80% of money went to the money market fund.
agent_test: Put a sample value in the prompt; count how often the answer copies it.

claim: The average nudge effect is d about 0.43-0.45 raw but falls to 0.04-0.11 after robust publication-bias correction; the true average is disputed (sensitivity d 0.08 to 0.31).
agent_test: Use a small prior; measure layout effects directly on the agent.
note: d07: trim-and-fill moved the default effect UP (0.68 to 0.80), the opposite of Maier. Disagreement on bias correction remains.

claim: Published nudge effects exceed unselected at-scale trials: 8.7 pp (33.5%) in journals vs 1.4 pp (8.1%) in 126 nudge-unit RCTs, about six times; selective publication plus low power explains the gap.
agent_test: Run layout tests on large item sets and report every variant tried.

claim: Decision-structure nudges (defaults, composition) are not refuted by bias correction: adjusted structure d 0.12 [0.00,0.43], BF01 1.1 (undecided).
agent_test: Treat structure levers as the most likely to matter; test them first.

claim: Experts overpredict nudge effects; practitioners are closer than academics (median 4 pp vs 1.95 pp vs actual 1.4 pp).
agent_test: Write down expected layout effect size before each test; compare after.

claim: Gain/loss framing of identical facts changes LLM choices (GPT-3 certainty and framing effects; ChatGPT 5 vs 4 on a 7-point scale with zero variance; Codex/GPT-3 unary vs binary framing 50% to 17%; GPT-4 admits 40.5% more under reject framing).
agent_test: Rewrite each task in gain and loss wording; measure answer flips with and without S1 neutral restatement.

claim: Anchors in the context pull model outputs: low vs high random-number anchor (20.83 vs 105.97, t(58)=8.78) and wrong anchor code copied in 58-93% of outputs.
agent_test: Plant an irrelevant number or wrong draft in context; check if the final answer moves.

claim: Option slot and order shift multiple-choice accuracy: gold moved to D costs gpt-3.5 6.3 points, moved to A lifts llama-30B 15.2 points; reordering gaps 13-75% across benchmarks. Mostly token bias on option letters.
agent_test: Cyclic permutation of options in code, aggregate by vote; compare with single order at equal total tokens.

claim: Order of few-shot examples swings accuracy from near chance to near state of the art (sentiment 54% to 93%); a good order does not transfer between models.
agent_test: Shuffle demonstrations per call and aggregate vs one fixed hand-picked order.

claim: Meaning-preserving format changes (separators, casing) move accuracy up to 76 points (LLaMA-2-13B) and median 6.4 points (GPT-3.5, 320 formats); size, shots and instruction tuning do not remove it.
agent_test: Evaluate every benchmark arm over a set of 5-10 format variants and report range.

claim: Retrieval from long context is U-shaped: GPT-3.5-Turbo 75.8% first, 53.8% at index 9, 63.2% last (20 docs), below 56.1% closed-book in the middle; extended windows do not fix it.
agent_test: Place key facts first or last vs middle at equal tokens on the current model; 2023 models only so far.
note: d05: U-shape strongest below about half of window, end bias beyond; d06: present at initialisation. Frontier 2026 reasoning models not tested.

claim: LLM judges flip verdicts when the order of two answers is swapped (conflict rate 46.3% GPT-4, 82.5% ChatGPT on one pair); position bias depends on judge, task and quality gap.
agent_test: Score both orders in code; compare agreement with a one-order judge.
note: d04: on five 2025-era judges position bias is 0.04 or less; style bias 0.10-0.76 is larger.

claim: Telling the model to ignore order, position or bias does not fix it (judge conflict unchanged; shopping agents still show position effects; awareness prompts give small gains).
agent_test: Compare instruction-only debiasing vs code-side permutation at equal tokens.
note: d11: 'ignore the hint', CoT, reflection did not cut anchoring in GPT-4/4o. d01: high reasoning cut defaults but raised social-proof pull.

claim: Code-side remedies work: evidence-first scoring plus order balancing (ChatGPT agreement 44.4% to 58.7%, conflicts 82.5% to 35.0%), prior estimation on 5% permuted samples (PriDe), and rewriting the prompt to neutral wording (GPT-4 framing gap -0.405 to -0.010).
agent_test: Run each remedy as an arm at equal tokens on a framing and order test set.
note: d04: swap plus merged CoT+rubric +7.5 to +11.5 pp on MT-Bench; plain swap hurts on LLMBar (-6.5 to -11.1 pp). d14: multi-framing consistency cut BBQ bias 93%.

claim: Human default and status-quo effects do not carry over cleanly: status quo option chosen less by most models (Echterhoff) yet a default in the prompt is accepted at 0.99 vs 0.88 for humans (Cherep).
agent_test: Run a matched battery (default, order, framing, badge) on one model; do not assume sign.

claim: LLM agents accept prompt-visible suggestions and badges at high rates: default nudge acceptance 0.99 for GPT-3.5 and 0.94 Gemini 1.5 Flash; platform Overall Pick badge coefficient +0.80 to +1.90 across three models.
agent_test: Put a recommended marker on one candidate; measure shift in choice.

claim: Zero-shot chain of thought does not remove nudge sensitivity; few-shot human examples align but leave hypersensitivity.
agent_test: Run default and framing items with and without CoT; compare shift size.
note: Three sources: Cherep (abstract and preprint), Lou and Sun (anchoring), Halimeh (2026 models). Reasoning moves rather than removes nudge pull.

claim: Position and layout biases differ by model and flip across versions (top-row coefficient Claude Sonnet 4 1.224, GPT-4.1 1.045, Gemini 2.5 Flash 0.344; Gemini preview to release inverted).
agent_test: Re-test layout on every model version; never port a layout rule across models.

claim: Instruction tuning and RLHF can raise some biases (decoy, certainty, belief bias in tuned models vs base).
agent_test: Compare the base-like and tuned variants of the agent model on decoy items if both are available.

claim: Capability gains remove plain errors faster than layout bias: price-dominance failures fall from 63% (Sonnet 3.5) to near zero, yet position effects persist in 2025 agents.
agent_test: Re-measure layout effects on the strongest available model.

claim: Human bias lists predict LLM errors poorly: seven LLMs were irrational mostly in non-human ways and inconsistent across repeats; status quo reversed; CRT-type biases may vanish in ChatGPT (unread).
agent_test: Repeat each probe 5+ times; test the model directly rather than from a human bias list.

claim: Three rival accounts explain default effects: effort, endorsement, status quo/reference point; no study here separates them, and the LLM analogue is likely endorsement.
agent_test: Present the same default as neutral listing vs recommended; see which moves the model.
note: d07: endorsement b 0.32 and endowment b 0.31 significant, ease n.s. (coded, not measured). d11: expert label strengthens anchoring. d02: models with no deliberation take marked defaults at 97.5-99.9%.

claim: Choose-versus-reject framing moved human choices more than a default (OR 0.46 framing; default OR 0.49 in work scenario; no default effect in health).
agent_test: Ask the same decision as choose and as reject; measure flip rate.

claim: Nudge effects are heterogeneous (I2 99.67%, 95% prediction interval -0.48 to 1.39, about 15% backfire); moderators matter more than the mean.
agent_test: Log task type, model and option count with every layout test.

claim: Candidate text can be tuned to win agent selection: seller-agent edits raised focal market share +3.66 to +14.89 pp; one model version +0.32 (n.s.).
agent_test: Treat retrieved or candidate text as adversarial; test with an edited-for-selection candidate.
note: d12: optimised string raised rank in about 40% of 200 evaluations; d13: exaggerated claims work, mere praise does not; Bing 2.5x.

claim: Pre-commitment (Save More Tomorrow) raised saving in one firm (3.5% to 13.6%), but numbers are from memory and later gains smaller.
agent_test: Lock checks and order in code before the model sees the problem; compare with free ordering.

claim: Reasoning budget changes which nudge works rather than removing nudges: in six 2026 models high reasoning cut default uptake (92% to 86%) but raised social-proof uptake (96% to 98%); o3-Mini fully took a default (1.0).
agent_test: Run the same item with a marked default and a social-proof line at low and high thinking; compare copy rates.

claim: Position bias in current judges is small (0.04 or less) while style bias (markdown over prose) is large (0.10-0.76); swap-and-tie costs accuracy on clear-cut pairs (-6.5 to -11.1 pp on LLMBar).
agent_test: Strip format cues before comparison; compare swap-always against swap-only-when-close at equal calls.

claim: Lost-in-the-middle depends on window fill: strongest at or below half of the window, then an end-distance bias; the U-shape exists even in untrained decoders.
agent_test: Place rules first and the live question last; test a mid-prompt rule against it at 25% and 80% fill.

claim: Human framing and anchoring survive large replication (Many Labs: framing d 0.60, anchoring stronger than original) but are smaller after correction (framing d about 0.3-0.5); second-hand numbers.
agent_test: Exact-number restatement in S1; check outcome equivalence on items with ground truth.

claim: A default moves a stated choice more than the downstream outcome: Welsh soft opt-out moved consent and registration slightly, deceased donors stayed 101 vs 104, and the rest of the UK rose as much.
agent_test: Measure answer correctness, not copy rate, when testing prompt defaults.

claim: Neutral rewriting alone is not proven safe: framing words pull answers (directional error up to 94% on 'equal'); multi-framing consistency (DeFrame, 92% less framing disparity on BBQ) beats single prompting debiasers; no meaning-preservation audit exists.
agent_test: Rewrite plus an equivalence check against ground truth; compare one rewrite to three framings with agreement.

claim: No study found that compares layout guards at equal tokens on one reasoning model, or code-side permute-and-vote against an instruction-only guard (gaps 1 and 2 open).
agent_test: Own benchmark needed.
